title: Erdős Problem #378: Density of Squarefree Binomial Coefficients

problemStatement.formal: For each r, does the set of n for which C(n,k) is squarefree for at least r values of k have a natural density, and is that density positive?
problemStatement.plain: Erdős Problem #378 asks whether the density of integers n with C(n,k) squarefree for at least r values of k exists and is positive. The answer to both is YES, resolved via Granville–Ramaré (1996).
whyMatters: Connects the multiplicative structure of binomial coefficients to natural-density questions in analytic number theory.
The resolution isolates the deep analytic input (Granville–Ramaré density results) from elementary complementation arguments.

proven: Density exists: for every r, atLeastSquarefree r = {n | C(n,k) squarefree for ≥ r values of k} has a natural density (erdos_378_density_exists).
Density positive: that density equals 1 − d with d < 1, hence is strictly positive (erdos_378_density_positive).
Full resolution packaged as erdos_378 / erdos_378_answer.
Complementation lemma atLeastSquarefree_eq_compl and the density-of-complement bridge natDensity_compl are fully checked (0 sorries).
open: The two analytic inputs (existence of the exact-count densities η_m, and that the deficient tail carries density d < 1) are the deep content of Granville–Ramaré (1996); they are stated as axioms, not reproved. Mathlib does not contain this machinery.

insights: The whole resolution is complementation: 'at least r squarefree' is the complement of 'fewer than r squarefree', so its density is 1 − d, and positivity is exactly the d < 1 clause of the Granville–Ramaré tail estimate.

The deep content is purely the two density facts of Granville–Ramaré (1996); once granted, the Erdős #378 answer follows by elementary, fully-checked Lean arguments — so axiomatizing those two inputs is the honest and efficient architecture.

Positivity is the substantive 'yes': existence of a density is the easy half; that the density is strictly positive (the excluded tail does not have full density) is what makes the answer affirmative.
Mathlib lacks the Granville–Ramaré machinery, so these inputs cannot currently be discharged; the entry is correctly badged 'axiomatized' (axiomCount 2) rather than 'verified'.

Threshold r=0 boundary: atLeastSquarefree 0 = Set.univ, so the Erdos #378 density there is exactly 1, showing the universal upper bound natDensity_le_one (d <= 1) is sharp/attained — the top endpoint of the interval (0,1] in erdos_378_density_mem_Ioc.

The complement_density axiom bundles three claims: the density of {squarefreeCount<r} EXISTS, EQUALS Sum eta_m, and is <1. The first two are now DERIVABLE from the single existence axiom granville_ramare_density_exists via finite additivity of natural density over the pairwise-disjoint exact-count strata (natDensity_biUnion_of_pairwiseDisjoint + natDensity_exactlySquarefree_range). Only d<1 (positive mass in the high-count tail) is genuine residual literature content. A future session could split complement_density into the derived value + a strictly weaker 'tail positive' axiom.
